lane: Ad-tech: rewarded ads on the web, policy, and revenue by geo
headline: Rewarded ads work in a browser (Google H5 Games Ads / Ad Placement API, Ad Manager GPT, AppLixir, Playwire, Venatus/AdinPlay) but NO Google web product has server-side verification of completion ("Server-side verification is an app only feature and it is unavailable for web use"), so a web-first coin economy must treat every ad reward as spoofable and keep it cheap; the bigger business risk is not gambling policy (a no-cash, no-purchase coin trivia game is outside every "real-money" rule we read, and Google's "social casino" definition only bites if it looks like simulated casino/sports betting) but Google's own rewarded-inventory policy, which requires rewards to be "non-transferable" and "redeemable only within the publisher's platform": staking an ad-earned coin into a pot another player wins is arguably a transfer to a third party, so ad rewards should buy non-transferable entries/energy and pot coins should be house-minted. Rewarded eCPMs are roughly $12-20 US, $8-15 tier-1 EU, $8-10 tier-2 EU and $1-3 India for apps; web rewarded is quoted at $4-15 blended by the only vendor that publishes numbers. EU needs a Google-certified TCF 2.3 CMP (deadline 28 Feb 2026 already passed), US COPPA amended rule is in force since 22 Apr 2026, and India's DPDP forbids targeted ads to anyone under 18 with a 13/14 May 2027 deadline. India's 2025 online-gaming Act defines "other stakes" to include "coins and tokens equivalent or convertible to money", so the coin must never be purchasable, cashable or transferable to money.

findings.finding: Google AdSense H5 Games Ads is the only Google product that gives an ordinary web publisher rewarded ads. It is by-application ('Access requires an application, and approval is subject to partner eligibility'), needs an approved AdSense account, and uses the Ad Placement API (adConfig()/adBreak()) with a 'reward' placement type.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/9959170 and /1705831; adsense.google.com/start/h5-games-ads: 'It is a by-application product... Account approval is not guaranteed.' Placement types doc: 'The Ad Placement API supports interstitial (including prerolls) and rewarded ads.'

findings.finding: In the Ad Placement API the reward is granted purely client-side: beforeReward(showAdFn) fires if an ad is available, adViewed 'called only for rewarded ads when the player completes the ad and should be granted the reward', adDismissed 'in this case the reward should not be granted'. There is no server callback, and the API (not the game) decides whether an ad shows, including 'An ad wasn't shown because the frequency cap was applied'.
findings.evidence: developers.google.com/ad-placement/apis/adbreak. Release notes (services.google.com/fh/files/misc/afgreleasenotes.pdf, last updated 18 Jun 2021) list 'Frequency caps can be incorrectly applied to rewarded placements' as a resolved issue and a client-side data-ad-frequency-hint parameter; the API 'takes care of deciding exactly when to show ads'.

findings.finding: Google Ad Manager 'rewarded ads for web' (GPT) exists for desktop/mobile/tablet web, but the help page states verbatim: 'Server-side verification is an app only feature and it is unavailable for web use.' Publishers 'are responsible for creating and displaying the screen where the user opts in to the rewarded ad, and for delivering the reward', must disable 'Block non-instream video ads', cannot submit multiple rewarded requests at once, and get three GPT events: rewardedSlotReady, rewardedSlotGranted, rewardedSlotClosed. Rewarded web inventory is eligible for reservations, Preferred Deals, Open Auction, Private Auctions and Programmatic Guaranteed.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/admanager/answer/9116812; developers.google.com/publisher-tag/samples/display-rewarded-ad; Ad Manager community thread 235861733 confirms no SSV on web. Ezoic technical guide (2 Mar 2026): 'Unlike mobile apps, web rewarded ads rely entirely on client-side events for reward delivery.'

findings.finding: Google's 'Policies for ad units that offer rewards' (identical for AdSense, AdMob, Ad Manager) is the policy most likely to bite FACT//DUEL, not the gambling policy. 'Direct monetary items may not be offered as rewards under any circumstance.' Allowed indirect rewards must be 'redeemable only within the publisher's platform' and 'non-transferable', defined as 'a reward that is only redeemable and usable by the same user who received it, and is not directly convertible into direct monetary items or items that can be transferred to a third party.' Rewarded ads 'must only be served after a user affirmatively and unambiguously opts in', publishers 'must deliver the promised reward(s)', and may not add text 'to mislead or incentivize users towards a particular choice (such as by indicating "watch this ad to support our business")'. Examples of allowed rewards include 'game character extra life' and 'loyalty rewards or points'. A coin earned from an ad, staked in a duel, and paid to the opponent is a reward that ends up with a third party; whether Google would read it that way is an interpretation, but the safe design is ad reward = non-transferable entry/energy, pot = house-minted coins.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/9121589; support.google.com/admanager/answer/7496282; support.google.com/admob/answer/7313578. The transfer-to-opponent reading is my inference from the text, not a Google statement.

findings.finding: Gambling policy does not prohibit this product as a publisher. Google Publisher Restrictions define 'Online gambling' as content that 'enables users to participate in online, real-money gambling or any internet-based game where money or other items of value are paid or wagered in exchange for the opportunity to win real money or prizes'. A restriction only means 'fewer advertising sources will be eligible to bid', and does not apply to users in the US, UK, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Ireland and others. Neither the Publisher Restrictions nor the rewarded policy mention 'social casino' or 'simulated gambling' for publishers.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/10437795 (also March 2025 change: restriction applies when gambling content is shown to users outside allowed countries).

findings.finding: 'Social casino' and 'simulated gambling' are advertiser-side and ad-category concepts at Google, but they define the shape the product must avoid. AdMob sensitive category: 'Social Casino Games are simulated gambling games (including, without limitation, poker, slots, bingo, lotteries, sports betting, betting on races, as well as other card games and casino games) where there is no opportunity to win anything of value'. Google Ads: 'Social casino games: Online simulated gambling-style games where there is no opportunity to win something of value'; 'Gambling: Staking something of value on the outcome of events or processes determined by an element of chance with the opportunity to win something of value'. A trivia duel is a contest of the player's own knowledge (skill), not a casino game or a bet on a sports event, so it is outside both definitions on their text. It only becomes relevant if FACT//DUEL runs Google Ads for user acquisition: since 14 Sep 2026 every gambling-and-games category (including social casino) needs certification, and 'sweepstakes casinos' were excluded from social-casino certification on 28 Oct 2025.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/admob/answer/3150953 and /6166400; support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/15132179; support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/17258294 (Aug/Sep 2026 update); sbcamericas.com 3 Nov 2025 on sweepstakes exclusion.

findings.finding: The WORD 'bet' matters for classification and for India, not for any explicit Google clause. Google's simulated-gambling list explicitly includes 'sports betting'; a sports app whose UI says 'bet coins' reads as simulated sports betting to keyword-driven ad-review, app-store review and India's advertising ban. No policy text we read hinges on the word, so this is risk management: use 'stake'/'entry'/'play for X coins'/'challenge' rather than 'bet', 'wager', 'odds', 'jackpot', 'casino', 'slots', and never show betting-like odds or multipliers.
findings.evidence: Inference from the definitions above; Google Ads social-casino certification requires games to 'include statements that they aren't offering or promoting real-money gambling and are not providing prizes of real-world value' (support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/15132179).

findings.finding: AppLovin publisher policy treats gambling as restricted, not prohibited: publishers 'may be permitted, in AppLovin's sole discretion' to monetize 'Gambling apps or websites, including online or offline lotteries, casinos, and sports betting, or real-money apps or websites' if they 'strictly adhere to any country- or region-specific laws'. It has no dedicated simulated-gambling or social-casino publisher clause; 'Infrequent/Mild Simulated Gambling' exists only as an ad-review creative category. Unity's Advertising and Monetization Services Content Policy (effective 30 Jun 2026) lists gambling and sweepstakes as prohibited by default with a restricted path requiring licences, age-gating and responsible-gambling messaging; it contains no text on virtual-coin trivia.
findings.evidence: legal.applovin.com/policies-publishers/; support.applovin.com rules-management-api; unity.com/legal/content-policy.

findings.finding: App-store rules: Google Play's Real-Money Gambling, Games and Contests policy is triggered only by 'real money (including in-app items purchased with money) to obtain a prize of real world monetary value'; its simulated-gambling clause ('must not provide simulated gambling content (for example, social casino apps; apps with virtual slot machines)') applies to apps that carry gambling ads. Its odds-disclosure text applies to 'loyalty programs' with 'variable, chance-based, or randomized reward systems' (disclose 'the odds... and the selection method'). Apple 5.3.4 covers 'real money gaming (e.g. sports betting, poker, casino games, horse racing) or lotteries'; 3.1.1 requires odds disclosure only for 'loot boxes... for purchase'; 3.2.2(x) expressly allows apps to 'incentivize users to take specific actions within apps (e.g. completing a level, watching an ad)'. Since 28 Jan 2026 Google Play requires apps with real-money gambling/games/contests features to use Play age-screening tools; FACT//DUEL with no money is outside that trigger.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9877032; developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/; Lexology note on the Jan 2026 age-screening enforcement (secondary).

findings.finding: India: the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025 (assented 22 Aug 2025) defines an 'online money game' as one played 'by paying fees, or depositing money or other stakes, with the expectation of winning monetary or other enrichment (irrespective of whether such games are based on skill or chance)', and 'other stakes' as 'anything equivalent or convertible to money, including virtual coins and tokens' (PRS: 'credits, coins, and tokens equivalent or convertible to money'). 'Online social games' are 'offered solely for entertainment, recreation, or skill-development' and 'must not involve any stakes or monetary gains in return of stakes'. Offering a money game: up to 3 years / Rs 1 crore; advertising one: up to 2 years / Rs 50 lakh. Rules 2026 notified 22 Apr 2026, in force 1 May 2026, with the Online Gaming Authority of India. An ad-funded coin that cannot be bought, cashed out or converted is not 'equivalent or convertible to money', but the coin ledger must be provably closed (no purchase path, no transfer to money, no prize of value) and the UI must not describe staking as betting.
findings.evidence: trilegal.com update on the Act; prsindia.org billtrack; mondaq/Lexology/newsonair on the Rules 2026 (22 Apr / 1 May 2026). MeitY and PIB PDFs returned 403 so the definition wording is from law-firm and PRS paraphrases.

findings.finding: Other web rewarded providers all exist and support rewarded on web: Playwire (web rewarded unit announced 8 Dec 2022; FAQ minimum 500,000 pageviews/month or 1,000 DAU for apps, majority US traffic; no CPM disclosed). Venatus (acquired AdinPlay in March 2023; 'purpose-built formats for browser game publishers'; minimums not published; approval 10-14 business days). AdinPlay (browser/.io game specialist, now Venatus). AppLixir (web-only rewarded video; 'requires a minimum of 5,000 daily active users'; supports 'iOS Safari and Android Chrome'; claims '$8-15 CPMs'; has a signed server webhook: 'POST a signed HTTPS request to a publisher endpoint after server-side validation of each completed ad', MD5 signature from a shared secret, plus a Reward Management System that 'limits the number of rewards per user within a dynamic 24-hour period' and 'enforces a minimum time gap'). AppLixir is the only web vendor found offering a server-side completion signal.
findings.evidence: playwire.com/blog/web-rewarded-video-ads and playwire.com/faq; videoweek.com 7 Mar 2023; venatus.com/publishers/browser-game-monetization; applixir.com/faq, support.applixir.com 'Step 5: Setting up Web Callback'.

findings.finding: Programmatic plumbing for rewarded on web is standardised: OpenRTB 2.6 added imp.rwdd ('whether the user receives a reward for viewing the ad, 0 = no, 1 = yes'), and Google Authorized Buyers fills rwdd 'identically to is_rewarded_inventory'. Playwire notes SSPs are still learning to categorise web rewarded inventory.
findings.evidence: iabtechlab.com OpenRTB 2.6 spec; support.google.com/authorizedbuyers/answer/11823046; playwire.com web-rewarded post.

findings.finding: Wrapping for the stores is the only way to get verified rewards. AdMob SSV callbacks carry ad_network, ad_unit, key_id, reward_amount, reward_item, signature, timestamp, transaction_id, user_id and custom_data, signed with rotating public keys (cache no longer than 24h); the Capacitor community AdMob plugin supports SSV (userId/customData) and 'SSV callbacks are only fired on Production Adverts'. AppLovin MAX S2S rewarded callbacks are HTTP GET with EVENT_ID and EVENT_TOKEN, 5-second timeout, up to two retries. Unity LevelPlay (ironSource) S2S callbacks require a userId set before init and a 200 response containing '[EVENT_ID]:OK'. Unity Ads S2S redeem callbacks use an HMAC-MD5 signature and must be enabled by Unity support. A TWA or raw WebView wrapper is the wrong vehicle: AdSense code 'may only be implemented on web-based pages and approved WebView technologies' (the WebView API for Ads), Apple 4.2 rejects apps that do not 'elevate it beyond a repackaged website', and Google Play rejects 'apps that only have limited functionality and content'.
findings.evidence: developers.google.com/admob/android/ssv; support.google.com/admob/answer/9603226; github.com/capacitor-community/admob; support.applovin.com S2S Rewarded Callback API; docs.unity.com LevelPlay server-to-server callback; docs.unity.com Unity Ads s2s-redeem-callbacks; support.google.com/adsense/answer/48182; developers.google.com/admob/android/browser/webview/api-for-ads; Apple guideline 4.2; support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9898783. Whether AdSense may run inside a TWA specifically is UNVERIFIED (community thread could not be read).

findings.finding: Consent, EU: since 16 Jan 2024 (EEA/UK) and 31 Jul 2024 (Switzerland) AdSense, Ad Manager and AdMob require 'a consent management platform (CMP) that has been certified by Google and integrates with the IAB's Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF)' for personalised ads; without a certified CMP traffic gets only 'non-personalized ads or limited ads'. TCF v2.3 (released 19 Jun 2025) makes the disclosedVendors segment mandatory for TC strings created on or after 28 Feb 2026. Google's own 'Privacy & messaging' European-regulations message is a certified CMP for web (AdSense/Ad Manager) and the UMP SDK is the app equivalent (Android, iOS, Flutter, Unity; no web SDK).
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/13554116; iabeurope.eu 'All you need to know about the transition to TCF v2.3'; developers.google.com/admob/*/privacy.

findings.finding: Consent, US: the amended COPPA Rule (90 FR 16918, 22 Apr 2025) had a compliance date of 22 Apr 2026, so it is fully in force; it expanded 'personal information', notice, security-programme and retention duties. On 25 Feb 2026 the FTC issued an Enforcement Policy Statement: it 'will not bring an enforcement action under the COPPA Rule against a Relevant Operator that collects, uses, or discloses personal information for the purpose of determining a user's age... without first obtaining verifiable parental consent', provided the data is used only for age verification, not retained longer than necessary, disclosed in the privacy policy, secured, and the method is 'likely to provide reasonably accurate results'; it 'intends to initiate a review of the COPPA Rule to address age-verification mechanisms'. A general-audience sports trivia site is covered only on 'actual knowledge' that a user is under 13, so the design rule is: neutral age gate, no child-directed marketing or art, no child-directed flag.
findings.evidence: ftc.gov coppa-age-verification-policy-statement.pdf (read in full); Davis Polk and Finnegan client notes on the 22 Apr 2026 date.

findings.finding: Consent, India: DPDP Rules 2025 were notified 13 Nov 2025; a 'child' is anyone under 18; Rule 10 requires verifiable parental consent via existing verified records or a government-issued 'virtual token mapped to the parent's identity and age' (DigiLocker); Section 9 bans 'tracking or behavioural monitoring of children' and 'targeted advertising directed at them'; consent-manager phase 13 Nov 2026; core obligations 13 May 2027 (Consently) or 14 May 2027 (Xident) - sources disagree by one day. For an ad-funded app this means India users must be age-assured as 18+ or served non-personalised ads only, and no profiling of under-18s.
findings.evidence: consently.in DPDP timeline; xident.io DPDP children article; EY India note.

findings.finding: Child-directed treatment is a revenue cliff. GameBiz Consulting (May 2026) measured COPPA traffic at '2.5 to more than 5 times lower eCPMs' than non-COPPA and states a misapplied child-directed flag costs '70% of your eCPM'; ironSource Direct's shutdown (30 Apr 2026) cut COPPA eCPMs a further 6-30%+. Google Play Families apps must use a self-certified ads SDK, call setTagForChildDirectedTreatment(true) and set max ad content rating G, and cannot transmit the advertising ID for children or users of unknown age.
findings.evidence: gamebizconsulting.com admon newsletter 11; support.google.com/admob/answer/6223431. Figures are one consultancy's own data.

findings.finding: Mechanics benchmarks: rewarded impressions per DAU 1-3 (revenuelab, Jun 2026), 'average of 2 views per DAU... healthy range 2-6' (coinis); completion 'often above 85 to 90 percent' (AppLixir, Aug 2026); AppLovin 2025 benchmarks cited as >90% completion; '9 in 10 players interact with rewarded ads' (Digiday via Mistplay, Nov 2025); suggested caps for casual games 6-10 rewarded views per session, 15-20 per day, with 60-120 s cooldowns (AppSamurai, 2025, unattributed); Unity data via Mistplay: users engaging with rewarded ads have 3.5x retention. AppLixir's worked example: 4,000 impressions at $8 eCPM across 10,000 DAU = $32/day, i.e. $0.0032 per DAU per day.
findings.evidence: revenuelab.fyi AdMob benchmarks 2026; coinis.com glossary; applixir.com benchmark 2026; business.mistplay.com rewarded-ads-stats; appsamurai.com rewarded ads best practices.

findings.finding: Avoiding ad-load complaints: Google Play's Better Ads Experiences policy exempts rewarded ads ('Since users have explicitly opted in to rewarded ad experience, these ads are allowed') but bans full-screen ads 'not closable after 15 seconds' and interstitials 'before the app's loading screen, when you start a level or during the gameplay'. AdSense H5 rules likewise bar full-screen ads 'after every user interaction' and during 'continuous game play and heavy user interaction'. The Ad Placement API itself frequency-caps. Design consequence: rewarded-only, offered at natural loss/empty-wallet moments, never forced, one prompt per duel outcome, plus a visible daily counter.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/12271244; support.google.com/adsense/answer/9959170.

findings.finding: Web-first has a structural ad-blocking tax that apps do not: GWI Q2 2025 puts global ad-block use at 29.5% of internet users (Backlinko), US at 32.5%, Germany near 49%, and US desktop (37%) far above US mobile (15%). Rewarded video on web is typically blocked along with everything else, so mobile-web-first mitigates but does not remove this.
findings.evidence: backlinko.com/ad-blockers-users; cropink.com; sqmagazine.co.uk (all aggregators citing GWI/Statista).

findings.finding: The live GitHub Pages build cannot carry AdSense: AdSense approves at parent-domain level ('uses the status of the parent domain for each subdomain') and platform subdomains whose parent the publisher does not own 'will never be able to complete AdSense setup'. A first-party domain is a prerequisite for any Google web ad product.
findings.evidence: github.com/google/site-kit-wp issues 8935/8124 quoting AdSense subdomain behaviour; support.google.com/adsense thread 180449812.

findings.finding: Revenue share on web: AdSense for Content pays 'publishers receive 80% of the revenue, after the advertiser platform takes its fee' (about 68% when the buyer is Google Ads); 'We don't disclose the revenue share for all AdSense products', and no share is published for H5 Games Ads.
findings.evidence: support.google.com/adsense/answer/180195.

recommendations.what: Restructure the coin economy so an ad never funds a transferable asset: rewarded ad -> non-transferable 'entries'/'energy'/practice unlocks tied to the account; duel pots paid from house-minted coins based on the result, never from moving the loser's ad-earned balance to the winner. Keep the existing coin/stake ledger separation and add a rule that ad-sourced units cannot be staked. Ask Google (AdSense/H5 Games Ads support) in writing whether staking ad-earned coins in a P2P pot is compatible with the 'non-transferable' clause before launch.
recommendations.why: Google's 'Policies for ad units that offer rewards' require indirect rewards to be 'non-transferable' and 'redeemable only within the publisher's platform'; a pot paid to an opponent is arguably a transfer to a third party, and this policy applies to AdSense, AdMob and Ad Manager alike.

recommendations.what: Purge betting vocabulary from UI, store listings and marketing: no 'bet', 'wager', 'odds', 'jackpot', 'casino', 'slots', 'multiplier'; use 'entry', 'stake'/'play for N coins', 'challenge', 'pot' sparingly; add a permanent 'coins have no cash value, cannot be bought or withdrawn' notice; never sell coins.
recommendations.why: Google's simulated-gambling definition names 'sports betting'; India's Act treats 'coins and tokens equivalent or convertible to money' as stakes and criminalises advertising money games (up to 2 years / Rs 50 lakh); keyword-driven review is the realistic failure mode.

recommendations.what: Buy a first-party domain, move the static build off github.io, apply for AdSense then H5 Games Ads (Ad Placement API 'reward' placement) as the web baseline; in parallel wire Ad Manager GPT rewarded as the upgrade path once there is a GAM account.
recommendations.why: AdSense will not approve a github.io subdomain; H5 Games Ads is by-application and is the only Google rewarded product available to a small web publisher.

recommendations.what: Treat every web reward as unverified: grant server-side only after (a) the server issued a short-lived reward nonce before adBreak, (b) adViewed/rewardedSlotGranted arrives within a plausible window (>= ad length), (c) per-account caps (e.g. hard 15-20 per day, 60-120 s cooldown, 1 per duel outcome), (d) device/IP velocity checks; price rewards low enough that a spoofed reward is worth cents; log every grant against the ledger.
recommendations.why: Neither the Ad Placement API nor Ad Manager web has SSV; only AppLixir offers a signed webhook on web.

recommendations.what: Ship a Google-certified TCF 2.3 CMP (Google 'Privacy & messaging' on web, UMP SDK in the wrapper) before any EEA/UK/CH traffic; implement a neutral age gate; do not flag the app child-directed; in India either age-assure 18+ or serve only non-personalised, non-profiled ads to unassured users, with DigiLocker-based verifiable parental consent designed in before 13/14 May 2027.
recommendations.why: Google requires certified TCF CMPs since Jan 2024 and TCF 2.3 since 28 Feb 2026; the amended COPPA Rule is in force since 22 Apr 2026; DPDP bans targeted ads to under-18s; child-directed treatment cuts eCPM by 2.5-5x.

recommendations.what: In AdMob/AdSense blocking controls keep 'Gambling & Betting (18+)' off (it is opt-in by default) and also block the 'Social Casino Games' standard category, at least for India and for any unassured-age traffic.
recommendations.why: India criminalises advertising online money games; gambling creatives in a sports trivia app invite regulator and store scrutiny.

recommendations.what: Plan a Capacitor (not TWA/WebView) build for Play and App Store using AdMob rewarded with SSV, mediated through AppLovin MAX or Unity LevelPlay with their S2S callbacks, as the second phase; keep the web build for acquisition and practice.
recommendations.why: Only app SDKs give signed completion callbacks; app rewarded eCPMs (US ~$12-20) sit above published web rewarded ranges ($4-15); Apple 3.2.2(x) explicitly permits incentivising 'watching an ad'; Apple 4.2 and Google Play limited-functionality rules reject website wrappers.

recommendations.what: Set instrumented targets: opt-in rate, rewarded impressions/DAU 1-3, completion >85%, ARPDAU by geo; offer the rewarded prompt only at natural loss/empty-wallet moments; show the remaining daily ad allowance in the UI.
recommendations.why: Matches industry benchmarks and Google's Better Ads Experiences and H5 placement rules, and pre-empts the ad-load complaints the competitor lane will surface.

recommendations.what: Model revenue with geo-weighted eCPMs (US $12-20, UK/DE $8-15, FR/IT/ES/PL $8-10, India $1-3 app; web 30-70% lower and ad-block-adjusted) and 1-3 impressions/DAU before committing to India as a launch market on ad revenue alone.
recommendations.why: India rewarded eCPMs are roughly a tenth of US and fell again in Q2 2026 (-5.18% Android QoQ).

recommendations.what: Once above 5,000 DAU, trial AppLixir (signed webhook) and approach Venatus/AdinPlay; consider Playwire only above 500k pageviews/month with US-majority traffic.
recommendations.why: Vendor minimums and the only web SSV-like mechanism found.

recommendations.what: Track the FTC's forthcoming COPPA age-verification rulemaking and India's OGAI guidance on 'online social game' registration; re-check Google's rewarded policy and the Ad Placement API terms quarterly.
recommendations.why: All three are moving in 2026-2027 and each can change the reward or consent design.

risks: Google rewarded-inventory policy: ad-earned coins moving to an opponent via the pot may be read as a transferable reward; an account-level AdSense/AdMob disable would end the business model overnight. Mitigation is structural (non-transferable ad rewards) and a written ruling from Google.

No server-side verification on any Google web rewarded product: coin inflation from spoofed adViewed/rewardedSlotGranted events, bot farms grinding ads, and invalid-traffic clawbacks against the AdSense account.
AdSense/H5 Games Ads application can be refused ('approval is not guaranteed'); the current github.io host cannot be approved at all.

Classification risk from the word 'bet' and sports theming: ad-review or store reviewers labelling the app simulated sports betting / social casino, which blocks Google Ads UA, invites Play/Apple review friction and, in India, could be argued to be advertising or facilitating a money game.

India: 'other stakes' includes 'virtual coins and tokens' convertible to money; any future coin purchase, gifting, trading or prize path would flip FACT//DUEL into an 'online money game' with criminal penalties; India rewarded eCPMs (~$1-3) may not cover serving cost.

Privacy: EEA traffic without a certified TCF 2.3 CMP gets only limited/non-personalised ads (sharply lower eCPM); COPPA actual-knowledge exposure if the sports art or contests attract under-13s; DPDP under-18 rule removes personalised ads for a large share of Indian users and demands DigiLocker-based parental consent by May 2027.
Web ad blocking (about 30% globally, near 50% in Germany, 37% US desktop) reduces fill and revenue; SSPs are still maturing their categorisation of web rewarded inventory.
eCPM data quality: most public figures are vendor blogs or aggregator re-quotes of Tenjin/Appodeal charts; treat all sub-country numbers as planning ranges, not forecasts.

Wrapper route risk: TWA/WebView wrappers face Apple 4.2 and Google Play limited-functionality rejection, and AdSense inside a TWA is unverified territory; a proper Capacitor build with native ad SDKs is extra engineering.
Ad-load backlash: interstitials during play or unclosable ads breach Google Play Better Ads Experiences and AdSense H5 rules; rewarded-only with visible caps is the safe design.
